anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : The submitted SQL, transaction, or batch logic forces the engine to touch far more rows, pages, or result bytes than the business task actually needs.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical devices or storage-virtualization layer cannot deliver the read/write bandwidth or IOPS demanded by the workload, so I/O queues and latencies explode.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : The free space on data, temp, or log volumes nears exhaustion, producing allocation failures, auto-extend stalls, or log-archive back-pressure.

When these three root causes strike together, the database exhibits an escalating mix of symptoms:  • SQL statements appear repeatedly in slow-query logs with highly variable and growing latency.  • Device-level and database wait statistics show both deep I/O queues and space-allocation waits.  • Temp, undo, and log segments bloat during the long-running queries, consuming the last remaining free blocks; auto-extend attempts pause behind already saturated storage paths, and eventually raise out-of-space errors.  • Checkpoints, log flushes, and writes from other sessions are starved, so even read-only statements see elevated latencies.  • Administrators observe contradictory signals—moderate CPU, but soaring I/O wait, shrinking space, and a flood of timeout and "cannot allocate extent" errors.

Causal chain: inefficient SQL logic creates large scans, wide result sets, and oversized transactions that bombard the storage subsystem with reads, spills, and writes. The surge in physical I/O quickly saturates the available throughput; as queues deepen, each I/O takes longer, stretching the lifetime of every open transaction. Prolonged transactions hold temp and log space for longer periods while simultaneously growing those areas, accelerating space depletion. As free space approaches zero, space-allocation failures force additional retries and background clean-ups, which in turn generate more I/O on the already throttled devices. The three anomalies therefore reinforce one another in a vicious cycle—heavy logic drives high I/O, high I/O inflates latency, inflated latency magnifies space consumption—culminating in widespread performance collapse and potential service outages.

entry.error_class: Class HV - Foreign Data Wrapper Error (SQL/MED)
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
